correctness.rationale: For the corrected metric-fit claim, central symmetry gives the projection body as twice a quarter-turn; the regular polar has vertex radius sec(alpha) and is offset by a half vertex step. Thus for 4|N the half-sector supports are p=2 cos u and q=cos(alpha−u)/c, 0≤u≤alpha; for N≡2 (mod 4) there is the known exact homothety. The square cosine and cosine-product integrals on a half-sector are (alpha+sc)/2 and (alpha c+s)/2, respectively. After multiplying by 2N and the support factors, the positive optimizer is C/B and its error A−C²/B reduces by the displayed difference-of-squares factorization. At scale 2c the signed uniform error decreases between the two opposite endpoint errors ±2(1−c); any other scale increases one of those endpoint magnitudes. This gives the unique Hausdorff scale and shows it exceeds the least-squares scale by a positive multiple of (1−c)(alpha−s). The asymptotics use alpha²−s²=alpha⁴/3+O(alpha⁶), alpha+sc=2alpha+O(alpha³), and 1−c=alpha²/2+O(alpha⁴). These proofs were checked for the exact supports, unnormalized dθ, and positive scalar domain. The removed angular formulas were mathematically valid as well: folding to a uniform half-sector and inverting 2c/(c+s tan u) gives their CDF, density, and uniform rescaled limit; removal is for prior coverage, not falsity.
residual_risks: Numerical grid tests cannot prove continuous optimization or arbitrary N. The analytic fit does not optimize over rotated, translated or affine copies.

value.rationale: The natural question is how the best scalar approximation to a projection body by its polar depends on the metric. Even on canonical regular polygons with the full symmetry group fixed, the angular quadratic and Hausdorff criteria do not agree on the scale. The exact gap in choices and leading error constants supply a benchmark for approximate polar-projection relations and prevent conflating two reasonable normalization criteria. This is a motivated pair of optimization problems, not a claim that changing variables in the earlier ratio law creates a new invariant. The removed probability corollaries did not justify a standalone repair.
residual_risks: This deliberately narrow comparison makes no claim of affine invariance, general stability, or improvement of a bound on arbitrary convex bodies.
